en: Hello.
Sasha, a highly contested three-set win.
We advance and move on.
Your thoughts?
Straight-set win, but anything
but straightforward in a way.
He played incredibly well,
fought incredibly well.
Second and third set,
I think it's more than obvious
that they could have gone both ways.
And I just played a few points better here
and there.
And I'm happy with the win.
Well, congratulations once again.
Questions?
You referenced not playing well
at the start of the tournament
when you were in your on-court interview.
Have you ever had a tournament
where you've started at a lower level
and made so much improvement across
the duration of it?
Because you've gone from, if it was low
for you, at an extreme height.
It's a great question.
I feel like when I made the final here
in 2020, I didn't play well,
but I didn't play well the entire tournament.
That never changed, funny enough.
And I made it to the final,
and I was two points away from winning.
But I think the improvement
has been quite dramatic for me.
And it's a great thing
because I really started off the tournament,
and I was like, well, this is pointless
because I'm not going to do anything here.
And here I am sitting and preparing
for a Sunday final.
So things like that can happen in sports
and tennis in general.
Things can change very quickly
for the positive or negative.
And for me, luckily, it was for the positive.
And now I'm going
to do everything I can to prepare
for Sunday.
Well done, Sasha.
Can I ask you about the ball bouncing?
It seems to be like I've really increased.
Yeah, I have no idea why.
I'm not doing it on purpose.
I just saw the stat.
I bounced it 12,000 times or something like
that.
That's quite funny.
I mean, are you trying to get it like a seven?
No, I'm not.
I'm not counting in my head.
I'm not getting a certain number
or anything like that.
I don't know why it increased so much.
I think today it decreased again
because I saw it before the semifinal.
So I was like, OK, it's got to go less.
But then I forget about it every once
in a while, and it goes up
to, I don't know what number it is.
What happens that makes you stop
and makes you be like, OK, now I got it out,
and now I can start?
No clue.
Honestly, like really honestly, no idea.
Just talk a little bit about these last six years
because obviously the 2020 final
is a very strange atmosphere.
Nothing going to be similar
to that on Sunday.
And just your own sort
of journey in these last six years
between US Open Finals.
Yeah, I think a lot has happened.
I've played in a lot of other finals.
I played a lot of big matches since then.
Back then, of course,
it was my first Grand Slam final.
I was inexperienced.
I was still a young guy, I would say.
Yeah, just different.
Everything is different.
And I am pretty sure that the atmosphere
is going to be very, very different on Sunday
as well, no matter who I play.
So what I'm looking forward
to that, I think it's going
to be a fantastic feeling playing a final
in a sold out Arthur Ashe
and not in an empty one.
Did 2020 leave any particular scar tissue
for you?
It did, until I won in Paris.
I think there was question marks,
there was doubts whether I was ever going
to win one for sure.
I talked about it quite openly
before, but now that I've won one, it's OK.
There.
Hi, Alexander.
At the end of last year,
you talked about the importance
of playing more aggressive tennis,
and that's shown itself,
particularly in the Wimbledon final
and many other matches this year.
When you're in the moment,
is that a conscious decision
or a conscious effort you have to make
to make yourself do that, like, say,
you did at the end of the match today?
I would say no.
I would say it's a conscious decision
that you're doing it
in practice every single day
so that it becomes automatic in a match.
In a match, you shouldn't think.
You shouldn't think
of whether I should make this decision now
or this decision now.
I think everything should just be a flow.
And the flow starts with how you practice
and what you do in practice.
It's as simple as that, because in tennis,
you've got a maximum amount
of one second between every shot.
You don't have time to think.
You shouldn't be thinking.
And I think it's about the practice sessions
that you do beforehand.
As you mentioned,
sold out at Ashe Stadium for Sunday.
You'll be facing an American.
We don't know which one yet,
but you have a very strong record
against both those players.
What are your thoughts
about them individually,
starting with Frances, please?
Frances is somebody that can do anything
with a tennis ball.
He can be aggressive.
He can also mess around with it a little bit.
He can be tricky to play, for sure.
I have massive respect for him.
Also, I've known him
for almost 20 years now, similar to Karen,
actually.
And Ben is just a big, powerful guy.
Massive serve, massive ground strokes.
Everything he does is just big.
They're a bit of a different style
of tennis player,
but they're both very exciting, I think.
Is the crowd a challenge
or something different for you?
No, I enjoy these kind of atmospheres.
I've said it before.
I mean, I played a lot of French guys
in France.
I think the most hostile crowd, if you call it
that, is when you're playing French
in Paris-Bercy back in the day.
That was quite intense,
and I always enjoyed those.
I always enjoyed those kind
of atmospheres.
Of course, I played Australian guys
in Australia.
I played Arthur Fery now in Wimbledon.
The Wimbledon crowd is a bit different,
though.
There's no question about that.
But for me, a loud and energetic crowd
is always great, as long as they're fair,
as long as they don't interrupt in the middle
of points.
I always enjoy these kind of atmospheres.
Last two in English, and then Matt.
Ciao. Congratulations.
You played also Italians in Italy.
But the general impression
is that you changed after you won the Paris.
Now you're more relaxed.
You smile much more, and so on.
And I saw smiling also your father
in these days.
Really, I didn't.
It's very rare.
It's very rare.
I didn't see that.
Yeah, so is also the team more confident,
I mean, more relaxed
when you are with your brother, father?
The old spirit have changed or not?
No, I think not much has changed,
to be honest.
I think, yeah, of course,
winning one was the ultimate goal.
But now we want more.
We want to achieve bigger things.
And we're still working very hard towards
that.
We're still very focused towards that.
And I think everybody has still a goal
in their vision.
Last question in English, Matt.
So you have more grand slam finals
than both Carlos and Jannik this year.
And you may actually end up
with more titles.
And then is that something you
would have thought might be possible back
in December?
I believed in it.
I believe that is possible.
I think not many of you guys did.
I think the question was always,
is Carlos and Jannik going
to play all four grand slam finals
between each other again?
Yeah, of course, a very legit question
with how the last two years went.
I mean, I'm happy with how this year went
so far.
But I got another big match on Sunday
and that's my focus.
Okay, let's switch to German.
Thank you. Thank you.
